titleStmt.title: History of the Zhou Dynasty · Shang 商

div.p: The Shang in the time of Wu Ding, about 1260 BC: the passage from the Middle Shang to Yinxu Phase I, the Zhukaigou people's move from the Ordos into Shaanxi, Wu Ding's campaigns in the Wei valley, and the first appearance of the cultures taken to be the Zhou.

Wu Ding's wars as the oracle-bone inscriptions and archaeology show them, from about 1260 to 1235 BC: the conquest of southern Shanxi, Zi Hua's fief in the east, the campaigns of Que, Zhi Guo, Fu Zi and Fu Geng in the west, the defeat of the Tufang and the offensive against the Qiongfang, and the southern expedition that secured the copper road against the Hufang and the Moufang.

The cultures appearing in the same span, under their own dates: in the north-east, about 1260 BC, the Weiyingzi culture succeeding the Lower Xiajiadian, and the Weifang type formed within the Weifang Phase III culture; on the middle Yangtze, about 1250 BC, the Miaotaizi type, one of the cultures identified with the Hufang, and the Lujiahe, Shidiba and Zhouliangyuqiao cultures.

The Late Shang about 1235 BC, at the opening of Yinxu Phase II: the rise of the Liujia culture and its people's move into the Zhouyuan, the Lijiaya and Xicha cultures and the question of the Guifang, the decline of the Dachengdun type, the Xiaobaiyang type, and the Wucheng culture.

From Wu Ding's last wars to the reforms of Zu Jia, about 1230 to 1150 BC: the end of the war with the Qiongfang and the decline of the Shilou type, the states of Bing and Xian in central Shanxi, the Heir Apparent Xiao Ji, the succession of Zu Geng and Zu Jia, and the withdrawal of Shang culture from the western Guanzhong.

The cultures appearing in the same span, about 1200 BC: in Korea, the end of the Misa-ri type, the stage of Garak-dong, Heunam-ri and Yeoksam-dong and the rise of the Beomui-guseok Phase II culture; and the Xujianian site of the Siwa culture.

The reigns of Lin Xin and Kang Ding, about 1150 BC: the Qiangfang's threat to the western lands and the eastward advance of the Liujia culture, the Zaoshugounao and Heidouzui types of the Chunhua region and the question of the Fang and the Xunyu, and the Bronze Age cultures of Qinghai and the Upper Zhangjiayuan culture.

The reigns of Kang Ding, Wu Yi and Wen Ding, about 1150 to 1088 BC: the wars with the Qiangfang and the other fang states of the west; the move of the Zhou under Gugong Danfu from Bin to the Zhouyuan, and the accounts of Taibo and Zhongyong; the Shang court's turn to the east and the salt-making settlements of the Bohai coast; and Jili's campaigns against the Rong and Di, down to his imprisonment and death under Wen Ding.

The cultures appearing in the same span, about 1100 BC: the Jiuzhan type of the Siwa culture; the Shuangfang and Xinchengzi cultures; in Korea, the Sinam-ri Phase II, Geumtan-ri Bronze Age Phase I and Beomui-guseok Phase III cultures; the Sanxingdui Phase IV culture; and the late period of the Xindian culture.
